column1:
Examples of possible gender-
focused outcomes for  
energy sector
column2:
Examples of questions to consider 
to formulate project strategies and 
gender-related design features

column1:
Enhanced energy-based income-
generating activities and women’s 
entrepreneurship in rural and 
urban areas
column2:
• 	Is	reliable	and	adequate	electrical	
and heating energy required for 
income-generating activities 
available in the target area? What are 
the constraints on access to energy 
faced by women?
• 	Is	it	possible	to	provide	the	energy	
economically? Will energy supply be 
affordable for the enterprises?
• 	Are	there	specific	occupations	that	
have been traditionally prevalent 
in the area that can be supported 
so that large number of women 
and men can benefit by improving 
availability of energy (e.g., village 
weavers or potters)?
• 	Can	there	be	discussions	with	
representatives and associations 
of mainstream industries for 
developing backward linkages with 
large number of small producers in 
the area?
• 	How	will	women	and	men	be	
informed about new opportunities?
• 	Do	women	have	the	capacity	to	run	
enterprises or do they need training 
and mentoring? Who will provide 
the training, how, and for how long?
column3:
• 	Develop	energy	projects	to	increase	
supply of electricity and other types of 
energy.
• 	Carry	out	awareness	programs	for	
residents, business community, local 
government representatives, and local 
officials on gender and energy issues, 
available and potential opportunities for 
participation of women in energy-related 
income-generating activities, and how 
more women can be involved in them.
• 	Partner	with	national	and	local	
nongovernment organizations (NGOs) 
and private companies to implement 
pilot livelihood programs. Activities 
can include training on use of labor 
and energy-saving appliances, and offer 
financial and business management, 
credit, market access, marketing 
strategies, etc.
• 	Conduct	skills	and	technical	training	on	
various processing, manufacturing, and 
maintenance technologies for running 
energy-based enterprises.
• 	Develop	regional	quality	assurance-
related services (e.g., testing of energy 
efficient stoves, solar lighting products) 
for businesses with potential for 
engagement of women.
• 	Arrange	for	capable	institutions	to	
provide initial mentoring and hand-
holding for the entrepreneurs, both 
women and men, and all aspects of 
running small businesses.
• 	Facilitate	linkage	with	government’s	
existing programs for promoting women’s 
entrepreneurship.

column1:
Institutional awareness raised and  
capacities built among government  
organizations for provision of 
gender-responsive services
column2:
• 	What	is	the	level	of	awareness	
of gender-energy linkages in the 
specific organizations?
• 	Are	those	involved	within	program	
planning departments adequately 
briefed on gender equity in energy 
issues?
column3:
• 	Build	gender	awareness	of	all	officials	by	
requiring attendance to targeted training 
programs and participation in action  
plan development.
